newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks weaker, Wall Street weighs.
newsitem.headline: German stocks weaker, Wall Street weighs.

text.p: German shares slipped in midday bourse trade on Thursday as the market caught up with late electronic market dealings on Wednesday, which were pulled down by weakness on Wall Street.
The 30-share DAX index was down 17.65 points, at 2,685.36 in early trade, while the IBIS DAX, which records day-long computer dealings, was up 0.60 points at 2,685.83.
"We're seeing a bit of caution with Wall Street down," said one trader.
Dealers said they did not expect dealings to be too active before the outcome of Thursday's Bundesbank meeting, although no interest rate movement was expected.
Most of the market interest focused on telecommunication and chemical sector shares.
Utilities firms Veba and RWE continued to rally after they said they would join forces with British-based Cable & Wireless to create a powerful challenger to monopoly Deutsche Telekom.
Veba gained 77 pfennigs to rise to 82.30 marks, while RWE was up 27 pfennigs at 60.87 marks.
Utility firm Viag continued to slide after RWE said on Wednesday it would pull out of talks on a partnership with the Bavarian company and British Telecommunications.
Viag lost five marks to trade at 576.00.
On Thursday Viag said it would still integrate with BT, despite the departure of RWE and shares in Viag, although weaker, were somewhat supported by the news.

Chemical companies Hoechst and BASF climbed in early IBIS trade, after Hoechst said the two companies planned an equal partnership joint venture to expand their activities in the market for polypropylene.
BASF also said it had formed a joint-venture with Shell International Chemicals Limited to produce polyethylene.
BASF was down 75 pfennigs at 49.20 and Hoechst was off 79 pfennigs at 57.73 marks and dealers said players were taking profit. "The sector is due for a bit of a sell off," said one.
